title: Stored XSS via SBOM component names assigned to element.innerHTML
rationale: Root cause: frontend/src/core/observations/Mermaid_Dependencies.tsx:111 assigns `createMermaidGraph(dependencies)` — a string built from unescaped, attacker-controlled SBOM component names (embedded via `id1("componentName")` at lines 83-84) — to `element.innerHTML`. The browser HTML-parses on assignment, so a component name like `` executes immediately, before `mermaid.run()` at line 112. Change 1 (line 111): assign to `element.textContent` instead of `element.innerHTML`. This is the canonical mermaid flow — `mermaid.run()` reads the node's text content (the code already clears `data-processed` at line 110 to opt into reprocessing), renders it, and replaces the element's content with the generated SVG. Using `textContent` means the diagram source is never parsed as HTML, so the assignment can no longer execute markup; payloads land as literal text characters. Change 2 (line 13): pin `securityLevel: "strict"` in `mermaid.initialize`. Defense in depth for the render step — strict mode runs mermaid's label output through DOMPurify and disables `htmlLabels`, so even if a component name survives into a node label, mermaid escapes/strips it in the produced SVG rather than emitting live HTML. It also blocks directive-injection via the `---config---` front-matter / flowchart syntax. The fix sits at the sink (where untrusted data crosses into the DOM). The deeper "sanitize on SBOM import" recommendation is a separate backend hardening change outside this frontend file and isn't required to close this DOM-level sink; the textContent + strict combination removes both execution paths at the rendering boundary.
variants_checked: Grepped innerHTML / mermaid.run / createMermaidGraph / MermaidDependencies across frontend/src. Only sink is Mermaid_Dependencies.tsx:111. The other uses of createMermaidGraph (lines 118, 129, 167, 169) flow through JSX children / react-admin LabeledTextField, which React escapes — not raw DOM injection. Callers ObservationShowOrigins.tsx:94 (origin_component_dependencies) and ComponentShowComponent.tsx:72 (component_dependencies) both feed the same component and are covered by this single fix.
bypass_considered: Tried a component name that closes the mermaid node-label quote and injects an HTML label, e.g. `pkg") --> bad`. Before the change this reaches innerHTML and the browser parses/executes `` at assignment time. After the change: (a) textContent never HTML-parses the string, so at assignment it is inert literal text; (b) when mermaid renders, securityLevel:"strict" routes the label through DOMPurify and disables htmlLabels, so the `` is stripped/escaped in the SVG instead of becoming a live element. Both the assignment-time and render-time execution paths are closed. A residual non-XSS effect (a malformed name corrupting the diagram layout) is a rendering-quality issue, not script execution.
test_note: No regression test added: the frontend has no test framework configured — package.json has no `test` script and no vitest/jest dependency or config, and there are no existing `*.test.*` / `*.spec.*` files anywhere under frontend/src. Adding a runnable test would require introducing a test toolchain, which exceeds a minimal fix. Suggested manual verification: render MermaidDependencies with dependencies `a("x") --> b` and confirm `window.__xss` is never set and no network request for `x` fires.
review_reason: The patch fixes the root-cause DOM XSS at line 111 by replacing `element.innerHTML = createMermaidGraph(dependencies)` with `element.textContent = ...`, eliminating HTML parsing of attacker-influenced component names (interpolated unescaped at lines 73/83-84) while preserving mermaid's intended behavior (mermaid.run reads the element's text). The second hunk adds `securityLevel: "strict"` to `mermaid.initialize` (line 12), defense-in-depth on the same mermaid instance against injection via diagram syntax. Both hunks are in the target file on the path from the sink to its callers (`origin_component_dependencies`/`component_dependencies`); no checks removed, no new surface, no suppression.
